title: Finite evaluation of the direct-image compositor
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, Operations o and Compositors c as in [def-sf-integral-system-operations], and m≥0. For arbitrary composable scheme maps f:X→Y, g:Y→Z, t:X→Z and h:f≫g=t, and every system M on X, the evaluation of c.pushComp(f,g) followed by the h transport and the push(t,M) coordinate equals push(g,push_f M), then the realized direct image of fixedPush(f,M), then the realized canonical fixed-scalar conjugate compositor and its h index transport. All coordinates are those of [def-sf-system-finite-evaluation-coordinates]; this has no open or constructibility assumptions.

source.place: Compactification-independence sentence: compatibility of individual refinement maps with counits and j_!, before the projection square is deduced. Integral-system realization steps 1 and 3 of lem-sf-integral-projection-refinement-square.

proof.text: The direct-evaluation counit equation, after cancelling the inverse-image evaluation isomorphism, identifies each direct evaluation with mateEquiv applied to the inverse pullback-evaluation square (private evaluation_is_mate).

Invert systemPullbackCompositorEvaluation as an equality of isomorphisms. Apply mateEquiv to this square equality. Mathlib conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp, mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp and mateEquiv_hcomp turn it into the intrinsic direct-image compositor square (private intrinsic_compositor).

Apply the intrinsic coefficient compositor normalization to the fixed-scalar presentation of the evaluated input. Naturality of the intrinsic compositor moves the inverse coefficient counit to its source. Paste the coefficient comparison square. Naturality of the next direct-image coefficient comparison and the coefficient-equivalence triangle identity cancel the middle realization; this gives exactly fixedPush in the second slot.
Substitute t using h. Both equality-index isomorphisms are identities by their definitions, reducing the goal to the preceding compositor equation.

from.place: Proof, paragraph beginning "For an admissible exceptional adjoint", sentence "the projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection] is a composite of precisely these tensor and counit maps, hence is equivariant as well": the Frobenius-transported compactification differs from the chosen one, so the two projection composites must be compared through the refinement comparison. Individual-arrow integral system realization of these tensor and counit maps, before their compactification comparison square is deduced. The one-input support/refinement part of the individual-arrow normalization, independent of tensor and projection. Finite scalar coordinates of the one-input support/refinement argument. Operation-level finite-evaluation factor, before the two factors are pasted.

lean.statement:
theorem compositor (o : Operations l E)
    (c : Compositors l E o) (m : ℕ)
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (t : X ⟶ Z)
    (h : f ≫ g = t) (M : System l E X) :
    let A := ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (m + 1))
    let RZ := sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence Z (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (m + 1))
    (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E Z m).map
        ((c.pushComp l E f g).hom.app M ≫
          (eqToIso (congrArg (Operations.push l E o) h)).hom.app M) ≫
      (push l E o m t M).hom =
    (push l E o m g ((Operations.push l E o f).obj M)).hom ≫
      RZ.functor.map ((ProperOpenPush A g).map (fixedPush l E o m f M).hom) ≫
      RZ.functor.map
        ((conjugateIsoEquiv
          ((derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) g).comp
            (derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f))
          (derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (f ≫ g))
          (leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f g)).hom.app
            (input l E m X M) ≫
          (indexIso (ProperOpenPush A) h).hom.app (input l E m X M))
